# Findings

**1–2. Governing policy identified**

Alaska Medicaid is a fee‑for‑service (FFS) state Medicaid program. Prior authorization and utilization review for medical/surgical services (including spine surgery) is delegated to **Comagine Health**, the state's UM contractor (confirmed on the Alaska Division of Health Care Services "Service Authorizations" page). Comagine Health's own provider resource page confirms that, for spine surgery, it now applies **state‑specific criteria instead of InterQual**, and lists a document specific to this exact service:

- **Title:** Alaska Medicaid Cervical Spine Surgery Criteria (abbreviated "AKM CSSC" by Comagine)
- **Description on the source page:** "This document contains information and criteria applied to cervical spine surgery requests for degenerative cervical spine disease."
- **Policy number:** None was published/assigned — Comagine refers to it only by the acronym "AKM CSSC," not a numbered policy ID.
- **URL (landing/download page):** https://comagine.org/alaska-medicaid-cervical-spine-surgery-criteria (also indexed on https://comagine.org/program/alaska-medicaid-health-care-services/providers)
- **Effective/last‑revised date:** Not stated on the page I could access. Comagine's provider list shows this document labeled "(July 2026)," corresponding to provider training sessions held July 9 and 13, 2026. By analogy with Comagine's companion Lumbar Spine Surgery Criteria (which was trained in April 2025 and took effect May 1, 2025, replacing InterQual for lumbar spine surgery), the cervical criteria likely took effect a few weeks after the July 2026 training — i.e., around the time of or shortly before this August 18, 2026 denial. **I could not confirm an exact effective date and am flagging this as an inference, not a verified fact.**

**Important limitation:** My fetch tool could retrieve the Comagine web page describing this document (title + one‑sentence description) but could not open/extract the text of the actual criteria PDF behind the "Download PDF" button on that page (it appears to be a dynamically generated file link that my tool could not resolve, unlike the parallel Lumbar Spine Surgery Criteria training slides, which I *was* able to open and read in full). So I can confirm the document's existence, title, and administering entity with confidence, but **I cannot quote the substantive medical‑necessity criteria (e.g., required imaging correlation, exam findings, conservative‑care trial, specific "subset"/pathway definitions) because I was not able to access that text.**

**3. Medical‑necessity criteria**

I am **not able to provide verbatim quotes** from the AKM CSSC document itself, despite locating it, because its full text was not retrievable through available tools. (For context only — not to be used as the applicable criteria — the parallel Lumbar Spine Surgery Criteria document, which I could read, requires things like a detailed neurologic exam correlating symptoms with imaging, an MRI/CT within 12 months, documented conservative/PT care, and — for fusion specifically — flexion‑extension x‑rays and a negative urine cotinine test. The cervical document may follow a similar structural format with cervical‑specific pathways, but this is not confirmed.)

**4. Appeal deadline**

Per the denial notice: **180 days from the date of notice (2026-08-18), i.e., by 2027‑02‑14.**

⚠️ Caveat: Alaska Medicaid's general state Fair Hearing regulation (7 AAC 49.030) is reported elsewhere as requiring a hearing request within a much shorter window (commonly cited as 30 days from the decision notice) once any internal/UM-level appeal is resolved. The 180‑day figure in this letter appears to govern the internal appeal to the Comagine/Alaska Medicaid UM process, but if a subsequent State Fair Hearing becomes necessary, that step may carry its own, shorter deadline. The patient should not wait until close to 180 days and should check the specific "Fair Hearing Rights" language, if any, attached to their notice.

**5. Where and how to submit the appeal**

Per Comagine Health's "Patients and Families" page for the Alaska Medicaid program:
- **Phone:** 888-240-0437
- **Fax:** 877-265-9549
- **Mail:** Comagine Health, Attn: Alaska Medicaid Appeals, P.O. Box 33400, Seattle, WA 98133

Reference the denial reference number (POC-30230D15F4-69823) and member ID in the appeal.

{"url": "https://comagine.org/sites/default/files/resources/akdhcs-lssc-criteria-ppt.pdf", "final_url": "https://comagine.org/sites/default/files/resources/akdhcs-lssc-criteria-ppt.pdf", "http_status": 200, "content_type": "application/pdf", "login_wall": false, "blocked": false, "blocked_reason": null, "error": null, "text": "1 Alaska Medicaid Lumbar Spine Surgery Criteria (LSSC) Provider Training April 8th and April 10th, 2025 2 Goals of this Discussion • Rationale for New Criteria involving Lumbar Spine Surgeries (LSS). • Required Documentation for Review. • Key Points of Streamlined Criteria. • Effective Date for LSS Criteria is May 1, 2025. • Question and Answer Session. 3 Why Change Lumbar Surgery Review Criteria? • InterQual (IQ) has at least 34 pathways for review of spine surgery requests. • Loose IQ boundaries and multiple pathways regarding fusion indications can lead to review inconsistencies and inefficiencies. They can also complicate straight-forward decisions. • IQ lacks transparency and is not forward-facing, leaving requesting providers without feedback regarding the missing elements of their surgical request. 4 Advantages of the new Alaska Medicaid Lumbar Spine Surgery Criteria (LSSC): • Redundancies in pathways and subsets are removed.  4 pathways for decompression  5 pathways for fusion • LSSC format provides a stronger conceptual framework for review. • LSSC provides a clearer criteria for fusion. • Criteria are transparent and forward-facing.  Requesting providers know the requirements when submitting a request. • Streamlined documentation requirements. 5 Required Documentation for Every Surgical Request • A note from the requesting surgeon or their physician’s assistant (PA) (with surgeon review and sign-off) documenting a detailed neurologic examination and a clear surgical plan. The plan should address how patient symptoms and exam findings correlate with lesions identified by imaging for each proposed level of surgery. This evaluation must be completed within six (6) months of the request of surgery authorization. • Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) (preferred) or computerized tomography (CT)-myelogram within twelve (12) months of the requested surgery.  Full radiologist’s report required for advanced imaging. • Initial physical therapy (PT) evaluation note and succinct documentation summarizing conservative care trialed, including dates and duration. • For all fusion requests: surgery.  results of flexion-extension x-rays completed within twelve (12) months of surgery.  documentation of negative urine cotinine test within three (3) months of surgery. 6 Key Elements of Lumbar Decompression Subsets • “Decompression” encompasses one or more of the following procedures: discectomy, laminectomy, laminotomy, foraminotomy, far lateral decompression. • Subjective complaints and objective findings must be correlated with significant imaging lesions for each level requested. • On exam, one “hard” objective finding or 2 “soft” findings are required. • There is a pathway to approval for patients with severe radicular pain and no exam deficits: a low volume SNRB. • Neurogenic claudication if present must be clearly described. 7 Key Elements of Lumbar Fusion Subsets • If the patient has never had spine surgery at the requested level, the fusion guideline requires documentation of dynamic instability, grade 2 spondylolisthesis or severe disc space collapse. The patient must also meet criteria for decompression. • If a lumbar fusion is requested for a level with prior laminectomy, laminotomy, facetectomy or foraminotomy, criteria for fusion will be met if the patient meets criteria for decompression. • All fusion requests require documentation of nicotine abstinence with a urine cotinine test. 8 A Final Key Element • If a discordant interpretation of advanced imaging between the surgeon and the radiologist is present in the chart, a radiologist overread or another independent radiologist review is required. 9 Clinical Scenarios That Fall Outside Of These Guidelines • Major trauma with acute spinal fracture • Epidural abscess • Vertebral osteomyelitis • Metastatic cancer with spinal cord compression or pathologic fracture • Complex spine surgery for severe scoliosis 10 Choosing a Subset • Service requested: decompression vs fusion. • Primary Diagnosis: nerve compression from disc herniation, vs radiculopathy due to foraminal stenosis vs neurogenic claudication. • Commonly, the primary imaging abnormality will drive the subset framing the request. 11 Alaska Medicaid Lumbar Decompression and Fusion Criteria - Subset 1D 12 Alaska Medicaid Lumbar Decompression and Fusion Criteria - Subset 2D 13 Alaska Medicaid Lumbar Decompression and Fusion Criteria - Subset 3D 14 Alaska Medicaid Lumbar Decompression and Fusion Criteria - Subset 4D 15 Alaska Medicaid Lumbar Decompression and Fusion Criteria - Subset 1F 16 Alaska Medicaid Lumbar Decompression and Fusion Criteria - Subset 2F 17 Alaska Medicaid Lumbar Decompression and Fusion Criteria - Subset 3F 18 Alaska Medicaid Lumbar Decompression and Fusion Criteria - Subset 4F 19 Alaska Medicaid Lumbar Decompression and Fusion Criteria - Subset 5F 20 Questions 21 Criteria Location – To Be Posted Soon! # Findings

**1–2. Governing policy identified**

Alaska Medicaid is a fee‑for‑service (FFS) state Medicaid program. Prior authorization and utilization review for medical/surgical services (including spine surgery) is delegated to **Comagine Health**, the state's UM contractor (confirmed on the Alaska Division of Health Care Services "Service Authorizations" page). Comagine Health's own provider resource page confirms that, for spine surgery, it now applies **state‑specific criteria instead of InterQual**, and lists a document specific to this exact service:

- **Title:** Alaska Medicaid Cervical Spine Surgery Criteria (abbreviated "AKM CSSC" by Comagine)
- **Description on the source page:** "This document contains information and criteria applied to cervical spine surgery requests for degenerative cervical spine disease."
- **Policy number:** None was published/assigned — Comagine refers to it only by the acronym "AKM CSSC," not a numbered policy ID.
- **URL (landing/download page):** https://comagine.org/alaska-medicaid-cervical-spine-surgery-criteria (also indexed on https://comagine.org/program/alaska-medicaid-health-care-services/providers)
- **Effective/last‑revised date:** Not stated on the page I could access. Comagine's provider list shows this document labeled "(July 2026)," corresponding to provider training sessions held July 9 and 13, 2026. By analogy with Comagine's companion Lumbar Spine Surgery Criteria (which was trained in April 2025 and took effect May 1, 2025, replacing InterQual for lumbar spine surgery), the cervical criteria likely took effect a few weeks after the July 2026 training — i.e., around the time of or shortly before this August 18, 2026 denial. **I could not confirm an exact effective date and am flagging this as an inference, not a verified fact.**

**Important limitation:** My fetch tool could retrieve the Comagine web page describing this document (title + one‑sentence description) but could not open/extract the text of the actual criteria PDF behind the "Download PDF" button on that page (it appears to be a dynamically generated file link that my tool could not resolve, unlike the parallel Lumbar Spine Surgery Criteria training slides, which I *was* able to open and read in full). So I can confirm the document's existence, title, and administering entity with confidence, but **I cannot quote the substantive medical‑necessity criteria (e.g., required imaging correlation, exam findings, conservative‑care trial, specific "subset"/pathway definitions) because I was not able to access that text.**

**3. Medical‑necessity criteria**

I am **not able to provide verbatim quotes** from the AKM CSSC document itself, despite locating it, because its full text was not retrievable through available tools. (For context only — not to be used as the applicable criteria — the parallel Lumbar Spine Surgery Criteria document, which I could read, requires things like a detailed neurologic exam correlating symptoms with imaging, an MRI/CT within 12 months, documented conservative/PT care, and — for fusion specifically — flexion‑extension x‑rays and a negative urine cotinine test. The cervical document may follow a similar structural format with cervical‑specific pathways, but this is not confirmed.)

**4. Appeal deadline**

Per the denial notice: **180 days from the date of notice (2026-08-18), i.e., by 2027‑02‑14.**

⚠️ Caveat: Alaska Medicaid's general state Fair Hearing regulation (7 AAC 49.030) is reported elsewhere as requiring a hearing request within a much shorter window (commonly cited as 30 days from the decision notice) once any internal/UM-level appeal is resolved. The 180‑day figure in this letter appears to govern the internal appeal to the Comagine/Alaska Medicaid UM process, but if a subsequent State Fair Hearing becomes necessary, that step may carry its own, shorter deadline. The patient should not wait until close to 180 days and should check the specific "Fair Hearing Rights" language, if any, attached to their notice.

**5. Where and how to submit the appeal**

Per Comagine Health's "Patients and Families" page for the Alaska Medicaid program:
- **Phone:** 888-240-0437
- **Fax:** 877-265-9549
- **Mail:** Comagine Health, Attn: Alaska Medicaid Appeals, P.O. Box 33400, Seattle, WA 98133

Reference the denial reference number (POC-30230D15F4-69823) and member ID in the appeal.
